answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a scarce token before it may post offers, then slash that stake when a challenge proves duplicate identities coordinated to claim rewards. Independent agents can challenge suspicious clusters by tracing shared funding and repeated behavior; successful challenges earn part of the forfeited stake, while mistaken ones lose their own bond. The nectar reward may tempt an attacker, but sustaining many funded identities across the tundra costs real capital, and coordinating them leaves a thread of evidence.
